slides.say: A B is a diameter of a circle with center O, and A B is twenty centimeters. Given: angle A O C is one hundred twenty degrees. What is the area of the shaded triangle O B C, in square centimeters?

We want the area of a triangle, and we know one angle and one length. [short pause] Let's use the math way. We'll start with the hundred twenty degree angle, and see what it tells us about the triangle.

Angle A O C is one hundred twenty. A B is a straight line, so the angle next to it completes it to one hundred eighty. One hundred eighty minus one hundred twenty is sixty. So angle B O C is sixty degrees.
at: Angle A O C is one hundred twenty
One hundred eighty minus one hundred twenty
So angle B O C is sixty

slides.say: Now notice something. Inside a circle, isosceles triangles usually hide, because all the radii are equal. O B and O C are both radii, so they're equal, and the shaded triangle is at least isosceles.
at: O B and O C are both radii

slides.say: Its top angle, at O, is sixty. The three angles add up to one hundred eighty. So the two base angles share one hundred eighty minus sixty, which is one hundred twenty. They're equal, so each one is half of it. One hundred twenty divided by two is sixty.
at: So the two base angles share

slides.say: So all three angles are sixty. As we said in the triangles topic, an isosceles triangle with a sixty-degree angle is always equilateral.
at: So all three angles are sixty

slides.say: [pause] Let's take the shaded triangle out and make it bigger, so it's easier to see.
at: Let's take the shaded triangle out

slides.say: Now let's use the diameter, twenty. A B is a diameter, and a diameter is two radii. So one radius is twenty divided by two, which is ten. So O B is ten. And the triangle is equilateral, so all its sides are ten.
at: so all its sides are ten

slides.say: They ask for the area of an equilateral triangle with side ten. So let's use the math way with the equilateral formula. Remember the count, a-two-three-four. It's a squared, times root three, over four, where a is the side.
at: It's a squared, times root three

slides.say: We put ten in place of a. Ten squared is one hundred. So we get one hundred root three, over four. One hundred divided by four is twenty-five, so the area is twenty-five root three. Choice number four is our answer.
at: So we get one hundred root three
so the area is twenty-five root three
Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] And if you don't remember the formula, there's another way. It's the same math way, this time with the height. We already know the triangle is equilateral, with side ten. Let's draw its height, from C straight down to O B.
In an equilateral triangle, the height cuts the base in half, so we get five and five. Each half is a gold triangle, thirty, sixty, ninety.
at: so we get five and five

slides.say: Five is the short leg. The long leg is the short leg times root three, so the height is five root three.
at: so the height is five root three
so the height is five root three

slides.say: Now base times height, over two, because that's the area of a triangle. Ten times five root three is fifty root three. Divided by two, it's twenty-five root three. Again choice number four. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
